modules.title: Welcome and our products
modules.short: Who we are, what we make

left.text: **Bharat Forge Aluminum** is part of the Kalyani Group, a USD 3.5 billion conglomerate with a global workforce of 10,000 people across Asia, Europe and North America. We are building the heart of the automotive industry in the heart of North Carolina.

Our mission is clear: craft high-quality, lightweight aluminum components that power the world’s top luxury vehicles. It reaches beyond production to environmental stewardship and social responsibility.

left.title: Our department in one line
left.text: We don’t cast, we don’t forge, but we finish!

right.cap: Kalyani Group footprint across Asia, Europe and North America

blocks.text: Our facility is designed to harmonize with nature, with a seamless connection between people and the environment. As leaders in forging we uphold precision engineering, customer focus and sustainable practice.

This manual gives new team members the **fundamental knowledge and awareness needed before working on the production floor**. It is also refresher training for current team members. It explains what we do, **why** each process is needed, why standards must be followed, and how your actions affect safety, quality, equipment, production and downstream operations.

blocks.title: The five training phases. Select a phase to see how you are released to the next one.

items.title: Classroom / training area
items.text:
**Method:** Department overview, hazards, quality, process flow and standard procedures.
**Release gate:** Knowledge check.

items.title: Demonstration
items.text:
**Method:** The trainer performs standard work and explains key points and reasons.
**Release gate:** You can explain the sequence and the risks.

items.title: Guided practice
items.text:
**Method:** You perform the work under direct supervision.
**Release gate:** No critical safety or quality misses.

items.title: Floor assignment
items.text:
**Method:** You begin normal floor activities with support available.
**Release gate:** Trainer and supervisor sign-off.

items.title: Refresher training
items.text:
**Method:** 30, 60 and 90-day observation and refreshers.
**Release gate:** Sustained safe, quality performance.

blocks.text: **Health, Safety and Environmental policy.** Bharat Forge is committed to providing the infrastructure, training and equipment to assure the wellbeing of our people and the environment, inside and outside the plant, and to comply with all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.
Finishing combines automated equipment, moving conveyors, rotating components, hot processes, material handling and forklifts. You must understand the hazards of your area before you work in it.

blocks.title: The most important rule
blocks.text: An unsafe or unclear condition is **never** treated as normal production.
Open each hazard to see what you need to understand and what can happen.

items.title: Moving machinery
items.text: Keep hands, fingers, clothing and body parts away from moving equipment.

items.title: Lockout / Tagout (LOTO)
items.text: Always make sure proper LOTO is followed **before** entering the machine area. Unexpected start-up can cause injury.

items.title: Forklift movement
items.text: Stay alert around forklifts, especially at intersections, blind corners, doorways and between machines.

items.title: Hot parts
items.text: Hot parts can cause serious burns and may stay hot even when they do not look hot. Always use the required PPE and proper handling methods.

items.title: Shot blast media dust
items.text: Aluminum dust is highly flammable and can create a serious fire or explosion hazard. Keep it away from flames, ignition sources and **contact with water**.

items.title: Abnormal machine condition
items.text: Unexpected sound, vibration, smell, motion, an alarm or damaged guarding all need attention. Report them.

items.cap: Lock on a machine isolation point
Fire extinguisher. Know where yours are and ask your trainer which type applies to aluminum dust.

blocks.title: Aluminum dust and water do not mix
blocks.text: Never use water on aluminum dust or shot media dust. Store them only in the specified containers that are free of moisture.
PPE is your first line of defense. Always wear the required PPE on the shop floor. Not complying can lead to disciplinary action. Select a card to see what each item protects against.
Wear all the time on the shop floor

items.title: Ear plugs
items.text: **Protects against** noise from machines and equipment.

items.title: Safety glasses
items.text: **Protects against** flying particles, dust, sparks, metal shavings and chemical splashes.

items.title: Steel-toe shoes
items.text: **Protects against** impact from falling objects, punctures from sharp objects and burns from hot surfaces.

items.title: Cotton clothing
items.text: **Protects against** melting onto skin. Cotton does not melt and stick to skin when hot grinding debris touches it.

blocks.text: Wear while working

items.title: Cut-resistant gloves
items.text: **Protects against** cuts from sharp objects and tools.

items.title: Face mask
items.text: **Protects against** inhaling dust, fumes and other airborne particles.

items.title: Face shield
items.text: **Protects against** flying metal particles and shavings hitting your face during grinding.

items.title: Arm protective sleeves
items.text: **Protects against** sparks and grinding dust while grinding.

quiz.why: Parts can stay hot without looking hot. Always use PPE and proper handling methods.

items.title: Help overburdened stations
items.text: Lend a hand to colleagues who are overwhelmed with workload. It builds a culture of teamwork and support.

items.title: Avoid idle time
items.text: Stay productive during downtime: help in other areas, organize your workspace, do 5S activities.

items.title: Cross-train
items.text: Learn tasks in multiple areas. You can fill in for each other, workflow transitions stay smooth, and the team stays adaptable.

items.title: Job responsibilities
items.text: Give 100% effort in every assigned task while strictly following safety protocols. Arrive on time and ready at the start of your shift. Arriving late without a valid reason can lead to write-offs and points that may lead to termination. Keep your work area and the company clean and maintain **5S**.

items.title: Accountability
items.text: Take ownership of tasks, meet daily and monthly targets, and communicate proactively about progress and challenges.

items.title: Quality policy
items.text: Only good-quality parts go to the customer. This protects the safety of end users: defects in parts used in critical automotive applications can cause catastrophic failures, injury or loss of life. Bad parts also damage the company’s reputation.

items.title: Continuous improvement
items.text: Share improvement ideas, concerns and feedback with colleagues, supervisors and managers, and take part in training and development.

blocks.title: Our quality promise
blocks.text: To consistently provide safe, high-quality products that meet or exceed expectations, while improving continuously for the benefit of all customers.

quiz.q: Your station is quiet while the next one is overloaded. What is expected?
o: Lend a hand, or organize your area and do 5S
quiz.why: Help overburdened stations and avoid idle time.

quiz.q: Why does cross-training matter?
o: People can fill in for each other and work flows smoothly
It lets you skip safety rules
quiz.why: A cross-trained team is flexible and adaptable.

quiz.q: Why do we only send good-quality parts to the customer?
o: Defects in automotive parts can cause failures that injure or kill people
quiz.why: End-user safety is the first reason. Reputation is the second.

quiz.q: What is 5S used for?
o: Keeping the work area clean and organized
quiz.why: Everyone is responsible for keeping the work area clean and maintaining 5S.

left.text: What is aging?
Aging is a special heat treatment that makes aluminum parts **stronger and harder**.
Why do we do it?

Aluminum is naturally soft and lightweight. For many automotive applications the part needs higher strength and hardness to perform safely and reliably. Aging gives the part its required mechanical properties.

left.title: Skip it and the part can fail
left.text: Without aging, a part does not reach the required strength and hardness. That raises the risk of failure in use.

right.cap: Aging furnace loaded with 8 baskets on the platform

blocks.title: Easy example: aging is like baking a cake
blocks.text: A cake needs the right temperature and the right amount of time. Too low or too high, or out too early or too late, and it will not bake correctly. Aluminum parts are the same.

blocks.cap: Why aging is critical. A missed aging step today can lead to a broken part tomorrow.

blocks.text: There are three steps. Select each one.

items.title: Loading
items.text:
- Parts arrive from Forging in a batch identified by a **unique number**.
- Load parts into wire baskets with the **fixed quantity and loading pattern**.
- Place wire baskets of a **single batch number** on the furnace platform.
- Put a **reference part with a thermocouple** in the basket. It monitors part temperature during the cycle.
- **Verify the batch number and quantity** before loading.
- Move the platform into the furnace by hand and close the door.
- Enter the batch information into the system, then start the aging cycle.

items.title: Heating
items.text:
- Once the cycle starts, gas burners heat the parts up to **189 °C (372 °F)**.
- That temperature is held for **two hours**.
- Then the furnace door **opens automatically** so parts cool naturally in air.

items.title: Unloading
items.text:
- Wait until parts have cooled to a safe handling temperature.
- Remove the reference part using the required PPE.
- Attach the **correct paperwork to each basket**. This keeps parts identified and traceable.
- Move baskets to the designated **WIP (work in progress) area** for the next process.

items.cap: Baskets lined up for the furnace

blocks.text: Drag the slider through one aging cycle. Notice what must be controlled: **temperature** and **holding time**.

blocks.title: Measurement Safety Critical Characteristics (MSCC)
blocks.text: For an aging furnace the MSCCs are **temperature and holding time**. They are the things we control and watch carefully so the heat treatment works well and safely.

blocks.cap: MSCC sign posted at the aging furnace

quiz.why: Aging is a heat treatment that increases strength and hardness.

quiz.q: What are the two MSCCs of the aging furnace?
quiz.why: Temperature and holding time are the primary Measurement Safety Critical Characteristics.

quiz.q: What temperature and hold time does the aging cycle use?

modules.title: Cleaning and penetrant at the LNR

left.text: The **Laubinger & Rickmann (LNR) machine** prepares forged parts for **Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI)**.
Parts from Forging may carry oil, dirt or other surface contamination. It must come off so surface defects such as cracks can be detected properly.

right.cap: Layout of the Laubinger & Rickmann (LNR) machine

blocks.text: Nine stages from loading to UV inspection. Select a stage.

items.title: Loading
items.text: Parts are **manually loaded** onto trolleys in the required loading pattern. The machine has **78 trolleys** of two types. Always use the correct trolley and follow the loading pattern for each product.

items.title: Ultrasonic cleaning
items.text: Removes oil, dirt and other contaminants. The tank holds a **citric acid solution** kept at **13 to 17 %** concentration.

items.title: Rinse 1, 2 and 3
items.text: Removes remaining cleaning solution and contamination.

items.title: Dryer 1
items.text: Dries the parts before penetrant is applied.

items.title: Penetrant
items.text: Parts are dipped in **fluorescent penetrant**. It enters surface openings such as cracks.

items.title: Wash 1, 2 and 3
items.text: Removes excess penetrant from the surface but leaves penetrant trapped inside defects.

items.title: Wet developer
items.text: Helps draw penetrant out of defects so indications are easier to see.

items.title: Dryer 2
items.text: Dries the parts before inspection.

items.title: Dark room / UV inspection
items.text: Inspectors examine parts under **UV light** for surface defects.

blocks.text: Which trolley?

opts.label: 200D, 910B, Audi knuckle
opts.detail: Use for the 200D, 910B and Audi knuckle parts.

opts.label: Redback, Bronco control arm
opts.detail: Use for the Redback and Bronco control arms.

left.text: **FPI is a non-destructive inspection method** used to find defects that are open to the surface and may be hard to see with the naked eye.
Penetrant enters small surface defects. After washing and applying developer, the penetrant trapped inside a defect is drawn back toward the surface.
Under UV light the indication glows brightly, so the inspector can find **cracks and other surface abnormalities**.

right.cap: A crack glowing under UV light

blocks.title: Where parts go
blocks.text:
**Acceptable:** shot blast feed conveyor.
**Reworkable:** rework conveyor, grinding, then the reinspection conveyor and inspect again.
**Non-reworkable:** scrap.

items.title: Before you start the machine
items.do: Make sure all the conditions shown by the red circles on the screen are green before starting the machine.
items.dont: Do not press any buttons on the screen, especially **Initial Chain Position**, without proper training.

items.title: Loading
items.do: Load parts at the loading area when the trolley is completely stopped.
items.dont: Do not load parts onto a moving trolley.

items.title: Bronco and Redback on the trolley
items.do: Load Bronco and Redback parts all the way inserted in the trolley and leveled at both ends.
items.dont: Do not leave Bronco or Redback parts partly inserted or uneven.

items.title: Marking a defect
items.do: Mark the defect with a **black marker**. Trace the marker over the complete defect.
items.dont: Do not use a red marker. Do not draw a circle around the defect.

items.title: Moving parts on the conveyor
items.do: Slide or push the part over the conveyor.
items.dont: Do not throw parts onto the conveyor. It can damage the part or the conveyor.

blocks.text: Safety bumpers

Safety bumpers stop the machine immediately in an emergency. Know where they are, and be careful **not to touch or hit them** without a safety reason. Locations: **inside the dark room** and **near the wastewater tote**.

quiz.q: Why do parts go through ultrasonic cleaning before penetrant?
o: Oil and dirt must be removed so surface defects such as cracks can be detected
quiz.why: Contamination hides defects from the penetrant process.

quiz.q: What concentration is the citric acid cleaning solution kept at?
quiz.why: The cleaning tank holds citric acid at 13 to 17 %.

quiz.q: Which trolley do Redback and Bronco control arms use?
quiz.why: The original trolley is for 200D, 910B and Audi knuckle. The T6 trolley is for Redback and Bronco.

quiz.q: What is the right way to mark a defect?
o: Black marker, traced over the complete defect
quiz.why: Use black marker, trace the full defect. No red marker and no circles.

quiz.q: A part has a defect that Quality has NOT approved for rework. Where does it go?
quiz.why: If the defect is not permitted for rework by Quality, the part is rejected and handled as scrap.

quiz.q: When can you load parts onto an LNR trolley?
o: At the loading area when the trolley is completely stopped
quiz.why: Never load onto a moving trolley.

quiz.q: What does fluorescent penetrant inspection do?
o: Finds surface-open defects that glow under UV light
quiz.why: FPI is a non-destructive method to find defects open to the surface.

quiz.q: What must be true before you start the LNR machine?
o: All conditions marked by red circles on the screen are green
quiz.why: Confirm every condition shown by the red circles is green.

After grinding, the part goes through the **reinspection conveyor** and **must be inspected again**.

items.title: Reinspection conveyor
items.text: After grinding, the part goes through the **reinspection conveyor**.

items.title: Inspect again
items.text: The part must be **inspected again** before it continues. Good parts continue to the shot blast feed conveyor.

quiz.q: Who decides which defects may be reworked by grinding?
quiz.why: Only defects approved for rework by Quality may go to grinding.

quiz.q: What happens after grinding?
o: The part goes through the reinspection conveyor and is inspected again
quiz.why: Reworked parts must be inspected again.

quiz.q: Which PPE do you add for grinding?
o: Face shield, arm sleeves, mask, cut-resistant gloves
quiz.why: Flying metal and sparks need face and arm protection.

o: Do not send it for grinding. Follow the scrap or MRB disposition

left.text: Shot blasting is a **surface-cleaning process**. Small blasting media are thrown at high speed against the rotating parts to remove surface contamination and give the surface condition the next process needs.

items.title: Feed conveyor
items.text:
- Parts from the LNR dark room are continuously loaded onto the feed conveyor.
- Always follow the **loading pattern in the One-Point Lesson (OPL)**.
- A **sensor** detects parts entering the machine.
- If **no parts are detected for 5 minutes**, the machine stops automatically.
- Keep a steady flow of parts whenever production is running.

**Why it matters:** correct loading and steady flow prevent unnecessary stops and keep production consistent.

items.title: Blasting machine
items.text:
- Parts enter directly from the feed conveyor.
- Inside, parts are **continuously rotated** so the whole required surface is exposed.
- Blasting media is thrown at high speed against the parts.
- The impact **cleans and conditions** the surface.
- Machine settings control the process for consistent blasting.

**Why it matters:** correct blasting cleans and prepares the surface by removing contamination and creating the required surface condition.

items.title: Discharge conveyor
items.text: After blasting, parts move onto the **discharge conveyor** and on to final inspection.

blocks.text: The wrong pattern can overload the machine and cause a **big breakdown**. Pick a product to see the right pattern and what the wrong one looks like.

items.title: Keep the feed conveyor loaded
items.do: Always keep the feed conveyor loaded. Keep extra parts in the WIP basket and use them when no parts are coming from the dark room.
items.dont: Do not overload the feed conveyor. Do not let it run empty when parts are available to load.

items.title: Place parts gently
items.do: Place parts gently onto the conveyors.
items.dont: Do not throw, slam or drop parts onto the conveyor. It damages both parts and conveyor.

items.title: Media and dust
items.do: Put shot media and media dust only in the specified containers, free of moisture and water.
items.dont: The media dust is flammable. Keep it away from ignition sources, sparks and water.

items.cap: Damaged conveyor bed. Throwing parts causes this.
Feed conveyor with a WIP basket alongside

quiz.q: What happens if no parts are detected by the sensor for 5 minutes?
quiz.why: Keep a steady flow of parts to prevent unnecessary stops.

quiz.q: How do you load 910B and 200D parts on the feed conveyor?
o: One long line with no gap
quiz.why: A random pattern can overload the machine and cause a big breakdown.

quiz.q: Bronco and Redback parts on the feed conveyor need…
quiz.why: Parts too close together overload the shot blast.

quiz.q: Is this loading pattern correct for Audi parts?
quiz.why: No gap overloads the machine. Audi parts need one space gap between them.

quiz.q: Is this the correct way to put parts on the conveyor?
quiz.why: Never throw, slam or drop parts on the conveyor. Place them gently.

quiz.q: Why must media dust go only in dry, specified containers?
o: It is flammable. Keep it away from ignition sources, sparks and water
quiz.why: Aluminum / media dust is a fire and explosion hazard.

quiz.q: The dark room is not sending parts for a while. What do you do?
o: Use parts from the WIP basket to keep the feed conveyor loaded
quiz.why: Keep extra parts in the WIP basket for exactly this situation.

left.text: Parts come off the discharge conveyor. In **Shot Blast 1** they transfer onto the exit conveyor and then to the inspection table. In **Shot Blast 2** they go directly to the final inspection table.
The visual inspector checks the **entire part** for defects or abnormalities such as:

blocks.cap: Discharge / exit conveyor of Shot Blast 1
Discharge / exit conveyor of Shot Blast 2

blocks.text: If a defect is found, the inspector marks the affected area and follows the right disposition.

items.title: Grinding / rework
items.text: Only defects **approved by Quality** for rework may go back for grinding.

items.title: Scrap
items.text: Defects **not permitted** for grinding or rework go in the designated **scrap basket**.

items.title: MRB / non-conformance
items.text: Parts needing a Quality decision go in dunnage with a **Hold tag** and move to the designated **MRB area**.

blocks.title: Acceptable part
blocks.text: When a part is completely inspected and confirmed acceptable, the inspector applies the required **soft stamp** and sends it to the **packing area**.

blocks.title: Important
blocks.text: Do not send a part for grinding unless the defect is specifically approved for rework by the Quality Department.

quiz.q: What does the visual inspector look at?
quiz.why: A thorough inspection of the entire part.

quiz.q: A part needs a decision from Quality. Where does it go?
o: Dunnage with a Hold tag, to the MRB area
quiz.why: MRB: parts needing a Quality disposition decision.

quiz.q: What marks a part as fully inspected and acceptable?
quiz.why: The inspector applies the soft stamp and sends it to packing.

quiz.q: Which defects may go back for grinding?
o: Only those approved by Quality for rework
quiz.why: Never send a part for grinding unless Quality has approved that defect.

quiz.q: A defect is not permitted for rework. Where does the part go?
quiz.why: Not permitted for grinding or rework means scrap.

modules.title: Packing
modules.short: Right tote, right hand, right label

blocks.text: Parts that are **fully inspected and soft stamped** are ready for packing. The packing operator puts approved parts in the **designated tote for that product**.

blocks.title: Never mix LH and RH
blocks.text: Always pack LH and RH parts in **separate containers**.

items: Verify the part / product before packing and use only the **designated tote** for that product.
Follow the specified **quantity per tote** (see the table).
Before moving a completed tote, verify the **part number, LH/RH orientation, quantity and correct traveler**.
Attach the required **traveler sheet** before moving a full tote from the packing area.
Label the tote with the **part name, part number, and LH or RH**.
Do not pack parts that are **damaged, unidentified, missing a soft stamp, or awaiting Quality disposition**.
Use proper **lifting techniques** and lifting aids.
Keep the packing area clean and organized to prevent mix-ups, damage and trip hazards.

blocks.text: Pick a product to see the container and the full pallet quantity.
Full reference table

items.title: Hand and product
items.dont: Do not mix parts of different product type or hand (LH and RH).
items.do: Pack only parts of the **same product type and hand (LH or RH)** together.

items.title: Labels and placards
items.dont: Do not keep labels and placards from the previous load. It leads to misidentification.
items.do: Remove all labels and placards from the previous load before packing. Put the correct placard on the container.

items.title: Soft stamp
items.do: Always check for a legible soft stamp and the right marking before packing a part.
items.dont: Do not pack parts without a soft stamp or proper marking.

blocks.text: **TPM (Total Productive Maintenance)** is about finding and reducing losses that stop us from producing **safely, at the required quality, and at the expected rate**.

blocks.title: What to do when you see an abnormal condition
blocks.text: Recognize it, report it, document it.
Do not accept repeated delays, small stops, rework or wasted movement as “normal”. Small losses repeated all shift add up to a big drop in daily output.
Filter by group, or search the list. Each loss has a plain-language meaning and a Finishing example.
Read each situation and pick the matching loss.

quiz.q: The conveyor keeps backing up and needs frequent resets. Which loss?
quiz.why: Short repeated stops interrupt production.

quiz.q: An operator walks far to get labels. Which loss?
quiz.why: Unnecessary walking, reaching or searching wastes time.

quiz.q: Checking the same area many times on good parts is…
quiz.why: More inspection than the standard requires.

quiz.q: Changing trolleys for a different product is…
quiz.why: Time lost preparing equipment for another product.

quiz.q: What is the response to an abnormal condition?
quiz.why: STOP → IDENTIFY → REPORT → DOCUMENT → CORRECT.

quiz.q: Furnace or compressed air running when not needed is…
quiz.why: Energy is used with no useful output. (Remember: bandsaw air valves OFF when not running.)

blocks.text: You are our last line of defense. Knowing what each forging defect looks like helps you protect the customer. Five defects follow. Each lesson shows an OK part next to a Not OK part where we have photos.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Never knowingly pass a defective or questionable part to the next operation. If unsure: stop, ask your team lead, confirm, continue.

quiz.q: Which defect is a raised area on the surface caused by entrapped gases or impurities?
quiz.why: A bunch of blisters makes a lamination.

quiz.q: What is shown in this photo?
quiz.why: Cracks are fractures or splits that compromise structural integrity.

quiz.q: Metal that did not fill the die cavity, leaving unfilled areas, is…
quiz.why: Underfill is the metal not completely filling the die cavity.

quiz.q: Which can be caused by thermal stress during heating or cooling?
quiz.why: Cracks: thermal stresses, excessive pressure or deformation, poor ductility or alloy.

quiz.q: Folding or overlapping of metal layers within the part is…
quiz.why: Causes include inadequate lubrication, die misalignment and excess pressure.

quiz.q: Layers of oxides or impurities inside the forged part are called…
quiz.why: Lamination comes from inadequate degassing, contaminants, or poor raw material handling.

quiz.q: What does this photo show?
quiz.why: The edge is not fully formed, leaving unfilled material.

products.name: 200D Wheel Carrier
products.what: The wheel carrier supports the **wheel hub and bearing** and connects the wheel assembly to the vehicle’s suspension.

products.name: 910B Knuckle
products.what: The steering knuckle supports the **wheel hub and bearing** and connects the wheel to the suspension and steering components.

products.name: Audi MLBW Steering Knuckle
products.what: The steering knuckle supports the **wheel hub and bearing** and connects the wheel to the suspension and steering components.

products.name: Redback Control Arm
products.what: The lower control arm connects the wheel assembly to the vehicle body or frame. It allows controlled wheel movement while helping maintain **stability and proper wheel alignment**.

products.name: Bronco Control Arm
products.what: The lower control arm connects the wheel assembly to the vehicle body or frame. It allows controlled wheel movement while helping maintain **stability and proper wheel alignment**.

underfill.name: Underfill
underfill.text: Underfill happens when the metal does not completely fill the die cavity during forging, leaving unfilled areas or voids in the finished part.

bad.cap: Not OK: edge not fully formed

laps.name: Laps and folds
laps.text: Folding or overlapping of metal layers within the forged part. It can weaken the structure.
causes: Inadequate lubrication between metal and dies
Improper die design or misaligned dies
Excessive forging pressure or inadequate support of the workpiece

bad.cap: Not OK: fold lines on the surface

cracks.name: Cracks
cracks.text: Fractures or splits in the forged part that compromise structural integrity and mechanical properties. Under UV light at the LNR, cracks glow.
causes: Thermal stresses during heating or cooling
Inadequate material ductility or improper alloy composition

bad.cap: Not OK: crack glowing under UV light

lam.name: Lamination
lam.text: Layers of non-metallic inclusions, such as oxides or impurities, inside the forged part.
causes: Inadequate degassing or refining of the melt before forging
Contaminants or impurities in the metal
Improper handling or storage of raw materials

bad.cap: Not OK: surface layers lifting and flaking

blister.name: Blister
blister.text: A raised area on the surface, generally caused by entrapped gases or impurities in the metal. A bunch of blisters makes a lamination.

finalExtra.q: Before you start work, you notice a guard on a machine is damaged. What do you do?
o: Stop, tell your team lead, and do not run until it is fixed
finalExtra.why: Damaged guarding is an abnormal condition. Stop, ask, confirm, continue.

finalExtra.q: What is the Stop, Ask, Confirm, Continue rule for?
o: When you are unsure about a process, part, machine, quality or safety condition
finalExtra.why: STOP the work, ASK your team lead or supervisor, CONFIRM the correct action, then CONTINUE safely.

finalExtra.q: A part’s flow in Finishing starts with…
finalExtra.why: Material from Forging goes to aging, then the downstream processes.

finalExtra.q: True or false: you may reset a machine fault yourself if it looks minor.
finalExtra.why: Escalate to your team lead or supervisor before acknowledging or resetting any fault.

scenes.vo: This is the aging furnace. Aging is a heat treatment that makes aluminum parts stronger and harder.

scenes.cap: Temperature and holding time are the critical characteristics
scenes.vo: Without aging, a part does not reach the strength and hardness it needs, and that raises the risk of failure in use.

Parts arrive from Forging in a batch with a unique number. Load them into wire baskets in the fixed quantity and loading pattern. Put baskets of a single batch number on the platform, verify the batch number and quantity, and place the reference part with the thermocouple in the basket.

scenes.cap: Platform in, door closed, enter batch info, start
scenes.vo: Move the platform into the furnace by hand and close the door. Enter the batch information into the system. When everything is verified, start the aging cycle.
Gas burners heat the parts up to 189 degrees Celsius, 372 degrees Fahrenheit. That temperature is held for two hours. Then the door opens automatically so the parts cool naturally in air.

items: Wait for a safe handling temperature
Remove the reference part wearing PPE
Move baskets to the WIP area
scenes.vo: When the parts reach a safe handling temperature, remove the reference part wearing the required PPE. Hot parts can cause serious burns. Attach the correct paperwork to each basket so parts stay identified and traceable, then move the baskets to the WIP area.

scenes.cap: Inform team lead, work order, Maintenance
scenes.vo: If there is a machine fault, follow the escalation chain: inform the team lead, the team lead puts in a work order, and the team lead contacts Maintenance. Never acknowledge or reset a fault without escalating it.
The bandsaw cuts the double-forged 910B knuckle. The right-hand and left-hand parts are made together, and the saw separates them.

items: Blade guard in place and tight
scenes.vo: Before you start, do all the start-up checks. Check the oil level. Make sure the oil valve and the air are on, the blade guard is in place and tight, the safety shield is available, and the blade tension is okay. If any check fails, do not run the saw until it is fixed.

scenes.cap: Seat it, secure it, start per standard work
scenes.vo: Load the part and position it correctly in the fixture. Make sure it is properly seated and secured. Start the cutting cycle according to the standard work instruction, and let the blade finish the cut before you touch the part.

scenes.cap: Remove carefully, check the cut area
scenes.vo: Carefully remove the part from the fixture without letting it touch the blade. Inspect the cut area for damage or abnormal cut marks. Then place the part in the designated WIP container or move it to the next process.

scenes.cap: Check for saw damage every time
scenes.vo: Sending a saw-damaged part to the next process can result in a non-conforming part reaching the customer. Always check the cut area before the part goes in the container.

items: Cut marks from touching the blade
No PPE: chips can fly off
scenes.vo: Watch for these. Cut marks happen when the part touches the blade during unloading. A cut in the wrong place comes from poor positioning. Check for blade wear. A part that is not secured is a safety hazard, and without proper PPE, chips can fly off and cause injury.
When the saw is not running, turn the air valves off.

The Laubinger and Rickmann machine prepares forged parts for fluorescent penetrant inspection. Parts from Forging can carry oil, dirt or other contamination. It must come off so surface defects like cracks can be found.
Before you start the machine, make sure all the conditions marked with red circles on the screen are green. Do not press any button, especially Initial Chain Position, without proper training.
The machine has 78 trolleys of two types. The original trolley is for the 200D, 910B and Audi knuckle parts. The T6 trolley is for the Redback and Bronco control arms.

scenes.cap: Load only when the trolley is stopped
scenes.vo: Load parts by hand in the required loading pattern, at the loading area, when the trolley is completely stopped. Never load onto a moving trolley.

scenes.cap: Bronco, Redback: fully inserted, level at both ends
scenes.vo: For Bronco and Redback parts, insert the part all the way into the trolley and level it at both ends.

The parts go through ultrasonic cleaning in citric acid kept at 13 to 17 percent, three rinses and the first dryer. Then penetrant, three washes, wet developer and the second dryer. Last is the dark room for UV inspection.
Penetrant enters surface cracks. After washing and developer, it is drawn back out. Under UV light the indication glows, so the inspector can see it.

scenes.cap: Mark defects with a black marker
scenes.vo: Mark the defect with a black marker and trace the whole defect. Do not use a red marker, and do not draw a circle around it.

items: Approved for rework: rework conveyor, grinding, reinspection
scenes.vo: After inspection a part takes one of three paths. Good parts go to the shot blast feed conveyor. A defect that Quality has approved for rework goes on the rework conveyor to grinding, then the reinspection conveyor, and must be inspected again. A defect not permitted for rework means scrap.
Slide or push parts over the conveyor. Do not throw them. It can damage the part or the conveyor.
Safety bumpers stop the machine in an emergency. They are inside the dark room and near the wastewater tote. Do not touch or hit them without a safety reason.
Some defects can be removed by grinding. Only defects approved for rework by the Quality Department may be reworked.
The inspector marks the defect location with a black marker, traced over the complete defect.
For grinding, wear your all-time PPE plus the face shield, arm protective sleeves, face mask and cut-resistant gloves. They protect against flying metal, sparks and grinding dust.
The marked part goes through the rework conveyor to grinding. After grinding it goes through the reinspection conveyor and must be inspected again before it continues.

scenes.cap: Not approved? Do not grind it
scenes.vo: Do not send a part for grinding unless the defect is specifically approved for rework by Quality.

Shot blasting is a surface-cleaning process. Small blasting media are thrown at high speed against rotating parts to remove contamination and give the surface condition the next process needs. The flow is feed conveyor, blasting machine, discharge conveyor.

scenes.cap: No parts for 5 minutes: the machine stops
scenes.vo: Parts from the LNR dark room are loaded continuously onto the feed conveyor. Always follow the loading pattern in the One-Point Lesson. A sensor detects parts entering the machine. If no parts are detected for 5 minutes, the machine stops automatically.
For 910B and 200D parts, load in a zig-zag pattern. A random pattern can overload the machine and cause a big breakdown.
For Bronco and Redback parts, leave enough gap between two parts. Too close together overloads the shot blast.
For Audi parts, leave one space gap between two parts. No gap overloads the machine and can cause a big breakdown.
Place parts gently on the conveyor. Do not throw, slam or drop them. It damages both the part and the conveyor.

Keep the feed conveyor loaded. Keep extra parts in the WIP basket and use them when no parts are coming from the dark room. Do not overload the conveyor, and do not let it run empty while parts are available.

scenes.cap: Flammable dust: no sparks, no water
scenes.vo: The media dust is flammable. Keep it away from ignition sources, sparks and water. Put media and dust only in the specified containers, free of moisture.
After blasting, parts move onto the discharge conveyor and on to final inspection.

items.cap: Shot Blast 1: exit conveyor, then inspection table
Shot Blast 2: direct to inspection table

scenes.vo: Parts come off the discharge conveyor. In Shot Blast 1 they transfer onto the exit conveyor and then to the inspection table. In Shot Blast 2 they go directly to the final inspection table.
The visual inspector checks the entire part, not just one area. Look for missing batch numbers, missing letters or markings, dents, cracks, underfill and any other visible defect.

items.cap: Not permitted for rework: scrap basket
Needs a Quality decision: Hold tag, MRB area

scenes.vo: If you find a defect, mark the affected area. Only a defect that Quality has approved for rework may go back for grinding. A defect that is not permitted goes in the designated scrap basket. A part that needs a Quality decision goes in dunnage with a Hold tag and to the designated MRB area.
When the part is fully inspected and confirmed acceptable, apply the required soft stamp. Then send the part to the packing area.
Do not send a part for grinding unless the defect is specifically approved for rework by the Quality Department.

videoSops.d: Right tote, right hand, right label

scenes.vo: After a part is fully inspected and soft stamped, place it in the designated tote for that product. The 910B goes in the Bharat Forge tote, 120 per full pallet. The 200D goes in the Bharat Forge tote, 60. Bronco and Redback go in the ZF tote, 54. Audi goes in a wire basket, 65.
Every product is made as left-hand and right-hand parts. Never mix them. Pack only parts of the same product type and hand together.
Before packing, remove every label and placard from the previous load. Old labels lead to misidentification. Then make sure the correct placard is on the container.
Check for a legible soft stamp and the right marking on every part. Do not pack a part without a soft stamp.

items.cap: Redback: no stab link, unique diamond shape in the middle
Bronco: has a stab link attachment

scenes.vo: Don’t confuse these parts. The Redback has no stab link attachment and has a unique diamond shape in the middle. The Bronco has a stab link attachment.

items: Label: part name, number, LH or RH
scenes.vo: Before moving a full tote, verify the part number, LH or RH, the quantity and the correct traveler. Attach the traveler sheet, and label the tote with the part name, part number and LH or RH.

scenes.cap: Do not pack: damaged, unidentified, no stamp, or waiting for Quality
scenes.vo: Do not pack parts that are damaged, unidentified, missing a soft stamp, or waiting for a Quality decision. Use proper lifting techniques, and keep the packing area clean and organized.

A.txt: For 910B and 200D parts, load them in a zig-zag pattern on the shot blast feed conveyor.
A.bad: Do not load 910B and 200D parts in a random pattern. It can overload the machine and cause a big breakdown.

B.txt: For Bronco and Redback parts, leave enough gap between two parts on the feed conveyor.
B.bad: If parts are loaded too close together, the shot blast will be overloaded and can cause a big breakdown.

C.txt: For Audi parts, leave one space gap between two parts on the feed conveyor.
C.bad: No gap between parts can overload the machine and cause a big breakdown.

Redback.t: The Redback part has **no stab link attachment**. It has a **unique diamond shape in the middle**, marked by the red circle in the manual.

Bronco.t: The Bronco part **has a stab link attachment**, marked by the green circle in the manual.

start.q: The inspector looks at the part. Is there a defect?

appr.q: Is that defect specifically approved for rework by the Quality Department?

np.q: What does Quality’s requirement say about this defect?

ok.t: No unacceptable defect. After the LNR dark room, load it onto the **shot blast feed conveyor**. After final inspection, apply the **soft stamp** and send it to **packing**.

rw.t: Mark the defect with a **black marker**, traced over the complete defect. Send it through the **rework conveyor** for grinding. After grinding it goes through the **reinspection conveyor** and **must be inspected again**.

sc.t: The defect is **not permitted for rework**. Put the part in the designated **scrap basket** and handle it per the applicable procedure.

mr.t: Put the part in **dunnage** with a **Hold tag** and move it to the designated **MRB area**. Quality decides the disposition.

Trainer performs standard work and explains key points and reasons.
Trainee can explain the sequence and risks
Trainee performs work under direct supervision.
No critical safety or quality misses
Normal floor activities begin with support available.
